12.3 Product Code Data Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No. 102, Product Code Data Segment. 
Note:  This segment can be used for all card types except for Comdata cards. 
Note:  This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 157 Adjusted Product Code Data.  
Merchants should send one or the other but never both. If both the segments are sent, the 
transaction will be declined. 
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Product Code Data Segment, the products 
within this segment must meet the following requirements: 
• Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. 
• For EV charging transactions, the EV fuel product code should be the first product code in 
the segment. 
• A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. 
• The total of product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts [Element 
No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 (Tax 
Amount) and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
• When tax product codes are included in the segment, the total dollar amount of tax products 
is also reported in Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
• All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data. 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchase. 
Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking 
(OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, 
DEF, REEFER), all on 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR 
require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes.  Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel 
fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product 
segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant 
information like quality, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant 
must ensure to send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as 
the very first product code within the Product segment. Refer to the Product Code Data segment 
for the details on the product information layout and rules. 
This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3.  (Please refer to 
section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) 
It has a maximum length of 381 alphanumeric characters (001–381/a–z/A–Z). 
It originates at the device. 
The following table illustrates the layout of the Product Data Segment: 
Notes: A Field Separator always follows Segment Type and Segment Length.  A Field 
Separator follows Product Amount when Product Amount is the very last element in the 
segment.  When a field is not populated, still send the Field Separator. 
 A Product Data Field Delimiter always follows Quantity and Unit Price.  A Product Data 
Field Delimiter follows Product Amount when Product Amount is not the last element in 
the segment.  When a field is not populated, still send the Product Data Field Delimiter. 
 For an example of this segment, please refer to Appendix B.  POS Purchase Example.

10.5.5 eWIC Transaction Processing 
This section discusses the following processing requirements for implementing the EBT version 
of Women, Infants and Children Nutrition Program solution (eWIC) for transaction processing 
involving BUYPASS: 
• eWIC Transaction Types 
• eWIC Prompt Codes 
• eWIC Payment Type 
• eWIC Authorizer 
• eWIC Totals 
• eWIC Product Data 
• eWIC Receipt Requirements 
10.5.5.1 eWIC Transaction Types 
Note: These specifications do not support Return transactions. 
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: 
• eWIC Authorization (a.k.a. Benefits Inquiry) 
This transaction enables an eWIC client to query the eWIC host for the following information: 
 eWIC client list of eWIC-approved products 
 eWIC client account balance information 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Authorization Response to the device. 
• eWIC Authorization (a.k.a. Benefits Inquiry) Cancellation 
This transaction cancels a previously submitted Authorization. 
Note: If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization 
Cancellation transaction is required. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Cancellation Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes 
the Request, and forwards the eWIC Authorization Cancellation Response to the device.  
The device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the Response. 
• eWIC Balance Inquiry 
This transaction enables an eWIC client to query the eWIC host for remaining eWIC account 
balance information. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Balance Inquiry Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Balance Inquiry Response to the device.  The device displays/prints 
the eWIC account balance information from the Response. 
  
--- PAGE 116 ---

Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-39 
The following nonfinancial transaction types are supported for eWIC: 
• eWIC Purchase Completion 
This transaction performs an eWIC client’s purchase. 
Note: If there is a time-out or the eWIC client cancels the order, an eWIC Authorization 
Cancellation transaction is required. 
This transaction is initiated by swiping an existing eWIC card at a POS device (device).  
When prompted, the eWIC client keys the necessary PIN into the device, and the device 
sends the eWIC Authorization Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and forwards the eWIC Authorization Response to the device.  The device displays/prints 
the eWIC account balance information from the Response.  The clerk scans the items and 
enters any applicable manufacturer/cents-off discount coupon amount(s).  The device sends 
the eWIC Purchase Completion Request to BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, 
and sends the eWIC Purchase Completion Response to the device.  The device receives 
the Response. 
• eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void 
This transaction guarantees reversal/void of the effects of an eWIC Purchase Request at the 
eWIC host when an eWIC Purchase Response is not received or is received “late” (a time-
out or a late response) at the POS device (device). 
Notes: This transaction must be completed (The eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
must be received by the device.) before any additional eWIC transactions can be 
sent from the device that originated the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request. 
If the eWIC host responds to the Purchase Reversal/Void Request, the Purchase 
Reversal/Void transaction is considered “processed” regardless of the Response 
Code. 
If no Purchase Reversal/Void Response is received, the Merchant must repeat the 
process at its earliest opportunity until a Purchase Reversal/Void Response to the 
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request is received. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that one of the following situations has 
occurred: 
 An eWIC Purchase Response has been received late; or 
 A time-out situation exists. 
The clerk sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request from the device to BUYPASS.  
BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the 
Response. 
  
--- PAGE 117 ---
 BUYPASS® Platform ATL105 Message Format Specifications 
 
 
 
 
Software Version:  ATL105 
Specification Release Version:    2026-3 
August 07, 2026 
10-40 
• eWIC Voucher Clear 
Note: This transaction is an optional transaction. 
This transaction allows the settlement of a previously authorized eWIC Voucher by 
electronically submitting—within established Merchant time limits—eWIC approvals received 
over the phone during a device/BUYPASS/eWIC host outage. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that the device/BUYPASS/eWIC host is 
offline.  The eWIC client’s purchase (including manufacturer discount(s)/cents-off coupons) 
is called in to the authorization center (center).  The center notifies the clerk whether the 
purchase is approved/declined. 
If the center declines the transaction, the eWIC client leaves. 
If the center approves the transaction, the center gives the clerk an eWIC Approval Number, 
and the clerk issues a paper eWIC Voucher to the eWIC client.  The eWIC Voucher contains 
the following information: 
 eWIC Voucher Number 
 eWIC Account Number 
 eWIC Approval Number 
 eWIC Transaction Amount 
Note: This information must be electronically submitted to the eWIC host within the 
Merchant’s specified time limit in order for the Merchant to receive payment. 
Using the information on the Merchant’s copy of the eWIC Voucher, the clerk keys the 
above information into the device together with any applicable manufacturer/cents-off 
discount coupon amount(s).  The device sends the eWIC Voucher Clear Request to 
BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends an eWIC Voucher Clear 
Response to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC information from the eWIC

10.5.6 Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) Transaction 
Processing 
This section provides information about support for the Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) to 
evaluate health and nutrition promotion in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program 
(SNAP). 
Electronic benefit card programs from some US states are offering HIP in order to award 
bonuses for healthy food purchases.  The goal is to provide an incentive to purchase a target 
group of healthy foods. 
The incentive for each purchase is calculated by the authorizer.  Running totals are maintained 
by the authorizer. 
Additional balances are returned providing the incentive earned for the transaction and month-
to-date incentive earned.  The balances are reset at the beginning of the fiscal month. 
A new data element (No. 164 [EBT Program Data]) supports this feature.  For a complete 
description of this element, please see section 13.2, “Data Elements in Data Element Number 
Order.”  Data layout examples for this data element are contained in appendix M, “Element 
Format Examples for EBT Program Data.” 
This new data element is used in the EBT Data Segment (Data Segment No. 103).  For a 
complete description of this addition, please see section 12.4, “EBT Data Segment.” 
The receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements,” also apply to HIP 
receipts. 
Please contact your Buypass representative for a list of states that support HIP.

10.5.2 Food Stamp Electronic Vouchers 
Electronic vouchers electronically submit food stamp approvals received over the phone during 
a device, BUYPASS, or authorizing host outage.  Electronic vouchers must prompt for the 
following items: 
• Account Number prompt 
• Approval Number prompt 
• Voucher Number prompt 
10.5.2.1 Account Number Prompt 
If the store system can retain the account information from an original transaction attempt, the 
remainder of the information can be entered at the controller level or directly into the device in 
the lane.  For stand-alone equipment, the electronic voucher transaction must allow for manual 
entry of the Account Number and the Expiration Date. 
In cases where the PAN is printed on transaction receipts, it must be truncated to its last four 
digits.  A series of X's equal to the number of truncated digits precede these four digits for a field 
length equal to the original Account Number's length. 
Example.  The Account Number 1234567890123456 prints as XXXXXXXXXXXX3456. 
10.5.2.2 Approval Number Prompt 
The device must allow for entry of the Approval Number received over the phone. 
10.5.2.3 Voucher Number Prompt 
The device must allow for entry of the Voucher Number from the manual voucher ticket.

eWIC host when an eWIC Purchase Response is not received or is received “late” (a time-
out or a late response) at the POS device (device). 
Notes: This transaction must be completed (The eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
must be received by the device.) before any additional eWIC transactions can be 
sent from the device that originated the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request. 
If the eWIC host responds to the Purchase Reversal/Void Request, the Purchase 
Reversal/Void transaction is considered “processed” regardless of the Response 
Code. 
If no Purchase Reversal/Void Response is received, the Merchant must repeat the 
process at its earliest opportunity until a Purchase Reversal/Void Response to the 
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request is received. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that one of the following situations has 
occurred: 
 An eWIC Purchase Response has been received late; or 
 A time-out situation exists. 
The clerk sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Request from the device to BUYPASS.  
BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends the eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void Response 
to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC account balance information from the 
Response.

Note: This transaction is an optional transaction. 
This transaction allows the settlement of a previously authorized eWIC Voucher by 
electronically submitting—within established Merchant time limits—eWIC approvals received 
over the phone during a device/BUYPASS/eWIC host outage. 
This transaction is initiated by the clerk determining that the device/BUYPASS/eWIC host is 
offline.  The eWIC client’s purchase (including manufacturer discount(s)/cents-off coupons) 
is called in to the authorization center (center).  The center notifies the clerk whether the 
purchase is approved/declined. 
If the center declines the transaction, the eWIC client leaves. 
If the center approves the transaction, the center gives the clerk an eWIC Approval Number, 
and the clerk issues a paper eWIC Voucher to the eWIC client.  The eWIC Voucher contains 
the following information: 
 eWIC Voucher Number 
 eWIC Account Number 
 eWIC Approval Number 
 eWIC Transaction Amount 
Note: This information must be electronically submitted to the eWIC host within the 
Merchant’s specified time limit in order for the Merchant to receive payment. 
Using the information on the Merchant’s copy of the eWIC Voucher, the clerk keys the 
above information into the device together with any applicable manufacturer/cents-off 
discount coupon amount(s).  The device sends the eWIC Voucher Clear Request to 
BUYPASS.  BUYPASS processes the Request, and sends an eWIC Voucher Clear 
Response to the device.  The device displays/prints the eWIC information from the eWIC

10.5.6 Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) Transaction 
Processing 
This section provides information about support for the Healthy Incentives Program (HIP) to 
evaluate health and nutrition promotion in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program 
(SNAP). 
Electronic benefit card programs from some US states are offering HIP in order to award 
bonuses for healthy food purchases.  The goal is to provide an incentive to purchase a target 
group of healthy foods. 
The incentive for each purchase is calculated by the authorizer.  Running totals are maintained 
by the authorizer. 
Additional balances are returned providing the incentive earned for the transaction and month-
to-date incentive earned.  The balances are reset at the beginning of the fiscal month. 
A new data element (No. 164 [EBT Program Data]) supports this feature.  For a complete 
description of this element, please see section 13.2, “Data Elements in Data Element Number 
Order.”  Data layout examples for this data element are contained in appendix M, “Element 
Format Examples for EBT Program Data.” 
This new data element is used in the EBT Data Segment (Data Segment No. 103).  For a 
complete description of this addition, please see section 12.4, “EBT Data Segment.” 
The receipt requirements listed in section 10.1.7, "Receipt Requirements,” also apply to HIP 
receipts. 
Please contact your Buypass representative for a list of states that support HIP.

12.30 Tax by Product Data Segment 
This section describes Data Segment No.143, Tax by Product Data Segment. 
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Tax by Product Segment, the following rules 
should be followed:  
• A Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) must be present in the transaction. 
• Each entry in the Product Code Data Segment (Data Segment No. 102) should have an 
entry in this segment too and the entries should be in the same order in both the segments.  
• Up to three taxes can be reported for a single product. If less than three taxes are to be 
used for a particular product, merchants can end the entry for that product early by using a 
field separator after the tax entry instead of a “\”. 
• If there is no tax associated with a particular product, the inclusive/exclusive flag should be 
set to “N”. In this case, the tax type and amount should be omitted. So, the entry for that 
product would only be the product number, followed by “N”, followed by field separator. 
• The only validation that will be done for this segment is whether the format is correct. No 
judgement will be made of the values contained. 
• For Canadian transactions, the valid values for Tax Type are GST (Goods and Services 
Tax), HST (Harmonized Sales Tax), and PST (Provincial State Tax). Any given product can 
have between 0 and 3 of these taxes specified in this segment.

12.41 Adjusted Product Code Data Segment  
This section describes Data Segment No. 157, Adjusted Product Code Data Segment. 
Note:  This segment is used exclusively and allowed for Comdata cards only. Any transaction 
containing this segment that is not for a Comdata card will be declined. 
Note:  This segment is mutually exclusive with segment 102 Product Code Data.  Merchants 
should send one or the other but never both.  If both the segments are sent, the transaction will 
be declined. 
Note: This segment does not allow any product codes above ‘899’ except for ‘955’ Cash Back. 
If any of these product codes is present, the transaction will be declined.  
When a Financial Transaction request includes the Adjusted Product Code Data Segment, the 
products within this segment must meet the following requirements: 
Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment. 
A maximum of ten products is allowed in the segment. 
The total of adjusted product amounts in the segment must equal the total of the amounts 
[Element No. 41 (Fuel Purchase Amount), Element No. 58 (Nonfuel Amount), Element No. 99 
(Tax Amount), and Element No. 17 (Cash Amount)] in the Standard Message Data Segment 
(Data Segment No. 100). 
Since tax amounts are being added to the individual product amounts, there should not be 
separate tax product codes included in the segment.  Instead, tax amount should be reported in 
Element No. 99 (Tax Amount) in the Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 
100). 
Since Discount, Tax, and Coupon amounts are being accounted for in the individual product 
amounts, there should not be separate discount, tax, or coupon product codes included in the 
segment. 
All fuel merchants must send fuel and nonfuel product data if applicable. 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchased. 
Note: With the growth of fleet industry and to fulfil the needs of the Over the Road Trucking 
(OTR) industry, BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple fuels (e.g., purchase of Diesel, 
DEF, REEFER), all in 1 transaction. It is estimated that up to 30% of fuel transactions in OTR 
require fill-ups involving multiple Fuel Type Codes.  Now, fuel merchants can allow multiple fuel 
fill-ups in 1 transaction. With the support of multiple fuels, a merchant must send the Product 
segment to BUYPASS with all the fuel codes and any non-fuel codes with all the relevant 
information like quantity, unit of measure, unit price, and product amount. Also, the merchant 
must send the primary fuel (fuel used for the primary fuel need of the truck/vehicle) as the very 
first product code within the Adjusted Product Code Segment. 
This data segment can appear in any of the fields in Data Section No. 3.  (Please refer to 
section 11.1, “Financial Transactions,” for additional information about Data Section No. 3.) 
It has a maximum length of 381 alphanumeric characters (001–381/a–z/A–Z). 
It originates at the device.

A Product Data Field Delimiter always follows Quantity and Unit Price.  A Product Data Field

Number: 1 Name: Access Code 
Character Type: AN Maximum Length: 12 bytes 
 
Representation: Variable length of up to 12 alphanumeric characters 
Purpose: Identifies data that must be dialed prior to dialing the phone

indicate a much longer than standard pause for use with phone 
systems that are slow to provide a dial tone.  In these cases, one 
or more B characters may be inserted in this element.  Each one 
should be interpreted as a 1-second pause.

12.49 EMV Terminal Floor Limits Data Segment  
This section describes Data Segment No.DL8,  EMV Terminal Floor Limits Data Segment. 
This new segment will contain floor limits for each card type (as RID) to be used by this 
terminal. Inclusion of this segment in a table load will be dependent on a Special set at the 
terminal level. This data will be maintained at the Buypass Host and when this data is changed, 
the table download flag will be set for all terminals that have this special set.
